saints.shortBiography: Elizabeth Ann Bayley Seton was born in New York City on August 28, 1774. She married William Magee Seton in 1794, and they had five children. After William died in Italy in 1803, Elizabeth’s encounter with Catholicism—especially her growing devotion to the Eucharist—led her to enter the Catholic Church in 1805. In 1809 she moved to Emmitsburg, Maryland, where she founded the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph’s and began St. Joseph’s School, helping lay foundations for Catholic education in the United States. She died on January 4, 1821. Pope Paul VI canonized her on September 14, 1975, making her the first native-born citizen of the United States to be canonized a saint.
saints.shortReflection: Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton’s life shows that holiness can grow through ordinary duties, loss, uncertainty, and courageous trust in God. Her devotion to the Eucharist transformed her search for truth into a life of service, education, and charity. When life changes unexpectedly, her example invites us to keep seeking Christ faithfully and to serve the people God places before us.
saints.prayer: Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton, you followed God through marriage, motherhood, widowhood, conversion, and religious life. Pray that I may seek Christ with courage, love the Eucharist deeply, and serve others faithfully in whatever vocation God gives me. Help me trust God when the path ahead is uncertain. Amen.
